context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local patch plan over existing AIWorkHub-owned modules (launch_queue_contract.py, launch_queue_persist.py, server.py, completion_inbox.py). No new external library/SDK/API surface is introduced; the MCP tool registration pattern (@mcp.tool() via FastMCP) is reused unchanged from 21 existing tools already in server.py, so no FastMCP doc lookup was needed.

tools/aiworkhub/src/aiworkhub/completion_inbox.py (build_completion_inbox: review_queue, stale_processing, runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts, read_errors facets)

key_finding_supersedes_b281_next_wave.finding: B281's next_wave proposed CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_QUEUE_REQUEST_TOOL_B282_V1 as a brand-new module (queue_request.py) writing to a brand-new log (mcp_queue_requests_b282_v1.jsonl). Direct inspection of the existing source tree (not listed in this task's read_first, opened because it is load-bearing for an 'exact API surface' plan) shows this would duplicate ~80% of already-built B119 infrastructure: launch_queue_contract.py already defines LaunchRequest/LaunchDecision/ProcessLogEntry/ResultHandoff plus enqueue_intent/evaluate_launch/describe_intent, and launch_queue_persist.py already provides an append-only JSONL persistence + read_persisted_log() read path, both wired into server.py as 3 read-only tools (aiworkhub_launch_queue_describe_readonly, aiworkhub_launch_queue_evaluate_readonly, aiworkhub_launch_queue_audit_summary_readonly).
key_finding_supersedes_b281_next_wave.recommendation: The MVP patch EXTENDS launch_queue_contract.py + launch_queue_persist.py additively (new optional dataclass fields, no removed/renamed fields) and adds ONE new write-gated MCP tool (aiworkhub_task_queue_request) that reuses the existing log path, instead of creating a parallel schema/log/module. This plan supersedes CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_QUEUE_REQUEST_TOOL_B282_V1 from the B281 next_wave file; see next_wave file for the corrected task card (renumbered B286 to avoid batch-token collision with this planning task's own B282 id).

mvp_patch_plan.principle: Additive-only. No existing dataclass field renamed/removed, no existing MCP tool signature changed, no existing test invalidated. LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED stays a hardcoded False constant in every new code path -- the MVP patch grants zero process-launch authority.

modify_additive_only.change: Add 4 new OPTIONAL fields to LaunchRequest (model: str|None=None, owner_prompt: str='', requested_at: str|None=None, stale_timeout_seconds: int=7200); add deterministic_request_id(task_id, runner, requested_at) -> sha1(f'{task_id}:{runner}:{requested_at}').hexdigest()[:16] helper (matches B281 section_1 request_id spec exactly); add 'duplicate_blocked' and 'rolled_back' to the decision string vocabulary returned by evaluate_launch (LaunchDecision.decision stays a plain str, no enum break). LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED, launch_enabled(), ProcessState members unchanged.

Extend _PROCESS_LOG_KEYS with the 4 new field names plus 'rollback_of_request_id' (str|None, default None) so _scrub_entry keeps them; add find_open_requests(task_id) -> list[dict] built on top of the existing read_persisted_log() (no new file I/O primitive, reuses the same read-only file open) to answer the duplicate-runner and idempotency checks. persist_transition/persist_intent signatures gain only new keyword-only optional args (backward compatible).

Register ONE new @mcp.tool() aiworkhub_task_queue_request (write-gated, mirrors the existing aiworkhub_task_auto_pickup write-gated pattern at server.py:56-60). Existing 24 tools unchanged; new total 25. No existing tool's parameters, docstring contract, or return shape touched.

new_files: tools/aiworkhub/src/aiworkhub/cost_ledger.py (B288: read-only aggregator, UNIONs launch_queue_persist log entries with core.usage_report())

api_surface_new_tool.name: aiworkhub_task_queue_request
api_surface_new_tool.gate: core.writes_allowed() / AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES=1 (identical gate name/semantics as every other write-gated tool in server.py; AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH is NOT sufficient by itself and is not read by this tool -- it stays scoped to the still-unimplemented launcher)

input_schema.adapter_id: str enum claude_cli|codex_cli|deepseek_manual, required, must be in launch_queue_contract.KNOWN_ADAPTERS
input_schema.requested_at: str|None ISO-8601 UTC, optional; server sets datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() when omitted
input_schema.request_id: str|None, optional; server computes deterministic_request_id(task_id, runner, requested_at) when omitted

output_schema.idempotent_noop: bool -- true when the same request_id already has a non-terminal entry (queued/planned/blocked_launch_disabled) in the audit log; matches B281 section_1 idempotency_rule
output_schema.duplicate_runner_blocked: bool -- true when a DIFFERENT runner already holds a non-terminal entry for the same task_id
output_schema.stale_recovery_requeue: bool -- true when completion_inbox stale_processing currently lists this task_id (marks the entry as a requeue, not a fresh launch)
output_schema.decision: LaunchDecision.as_dict() -- permitted is always false; state is always blocked_launch_disabled because LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED stays False
output_schema.persisted_entry: ProcessLogEntry.as_dict() extended, or null when write gate is closed or the request was an idempotent/duplicate no-op
output_schema.authority_flags: same shape as _launch_queue_authority_flags(), all false, write_gate_enabled mirrors core.writes_allowed()

api_surface_new_tool.reuses_existing_log: tools/aiworkhub/logs/launch_queue_audit.jsonl (AIWORKHUB_LAUNCH_QUEUE_LOG_PATH override) -- no new file, no new log format, append-only preserved.

mvp_patch_plan.queue_request_schema: B281 section_1 queue_request_envelope, realized as the aiworkhub_task_queue_request input_schema above; request_id generation matches B281's sha1(task_id + runner + requested_at)[:16] rule exactly via deterministic_request_id().

completion_inbox_integration.flow: Worker finishes -> taskctl.py review <task_id> -> completion_inbox.build_completion_inbox()['review_queue'] shows it (unchanged, B275 contract). Codex detects via existing aiworkhub_completion_inbox tool. No change required to completion_inbox.py for the MVP patch; stale_recovery.py (B287) is an ADDITIONAL consumer of the same build_completion_inbox()['stale_processing'] facet, read-only, no new taskctl call added.

safety_gates.G_WRITE_EXISTING: core.writes_allowed() / AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES -- reused unchanged; aiworkhub_task_queue_request behaves like every other write-gated tool: gate closed -> persisted_entry=null, no file write.
safety_gates.G_LAUNCH_EXISTING: launch_queue_contract.LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED stays a hardcoded False constant; AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH is read only for gate_status() reporting, never to permit a spawn. No code path in this MVP patch imports subprocess/os.exec/os.spawn/os.system/os.popen.
safety_gates.G_DUPLICATE_RUNNER: Before persisting, aiworkhub_task_queue_request calls find_open_requests(task_id). If any open (non-terminal) entry exists for a DIFFERENT runner than the requester, the call returns duplicate_runner_blocked=true and persisted_entry=null -- mirrors core.collision_guard()'s existing collision semantics, no new collision authority introduced.
safety_gates.G_STALE_RECOVERY: aiworkhub_task_queue_request cross-checks completion_inbox.build_completion_inbox()['stale_processing'] for the task_id; if present, the persisted entry is tagged stale_recovery_requeue=true instead of being treated as a first launch, preventing double-processing of a merely-stale (not dead) task.
safety_gates.G_ROLLBACK: Because the audit log is append-only (existing invariant, unchanged), rollback is a NEW compensating record: rollback_of_request_id references the original request_id and decision='rolled_back'. No delete/rewrite/truncate path is ever introduced; read_persisted_log() consumers can filter rolled_back chains.
safety_gates.G_USAGE_EXISTING: core.usage_report() remains the sole source of truth for token/cost counts; cost_ledger.py (B288) only aggregates (UNION + dedup by task_id/runner/model), it never writes usage data itself.

tests_plan: test_mcp_queue_request_tool_b286_v1.sh: write-gate-off default (persisted_entry=null); write-gate-on happy path (one JSONL line appended, all new fields present); idempotent resubmission (same request_id -> idempotent_noop=true, no 2nd line appended); duplicate-runner block (2nd runner, same task_id, different runner -> duplicate_runner_blocked=true, no write); LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED assertion stays False across every case; no subprocess/os.exec/os.system import anywhere in the new/changed source.

test_mcp_stale_recovery_orchestrator_b287_v1.sh: fixture stale_processing rows covering all 4 action types (requeue/mark_done/kill_zombie/escalate); asserts recommendations-only (no taskctl write command ever issued by the module).
test_mcp_cost_ledger_aggregator_b288_v1.sh: fixture launch-log + usage_report rows; asserts UNION/dedup correctness and zero file writes.

neural_bridge_note: This plan introduces no learned decision authority and no regex/keyword cue router as cognition. The duplicate-runner check, stale-recovery tag, and rollback record are deterministic support-boundary bookkeeping over an already-deterministic append-only audit log -- the same class of executor logic as core.collision_guard() and completion_inbox's batch-mismatch replica, not a routing/selection decision. Any FUTURE task that teaches a controller to PRIORITIZE which queued request to launch next, or to SELECT an adapter/model, remains scoped to MCP_NEURAL_LAUNCH_ROUTING_MIGRATION_V1 (already tracked in launch_queue_contract.py's module docstring) and is unaffected by this plan.
blockers: LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED_STILL_FALSE: no task in this plan or its next_wave flips LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED to true; an actual process-spawn implementation remains a separate, explicitly-gated future task (unchanged from B276/B281 framing).

PID_TRACKING_GAP_FOR_ZOMBIE_KILL: ProcessLogEntry has no pid field today; B287's kill_zombie action_type can only be a recommendation with confidence=low until a pid field is added additively (tracked as a B287 sub-task, not blocking this plan).

COST_FIELDS_GAP_FOR_LEDGER: ProcessLogEntry has no token/cost fields today, so B288's launch-log side of the UNION is empty until cost fields are added additively (core.usage_report() remains fully usable as the other UNION side in the meantime).
remaining_gaps_not_solved_by_this_plan: NO_PROCESS_SPAWN_IMPLEMENTED: unchanged from B281 -- still deferred to a future explicitly-gated task.
NO_TRUE_PUSH: detection stays pull-based (agent loop calls completion_inbox / aiworkhub_task_queue_request), unchanged from B281.
NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ: this plan and the tools it specifies operate on task-card metadata and the launch-queue audit log only, never artifact file contents.
